IN THE
Supreme Court of the United States

KALEY CHILES,
       Petitioner,
v.
PATTY SALAZAR, IN HER OFFICIAL CAPACITY AS
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF THE COLORADO DEPARTMENT
OF REGULATORY AGENCIES, ET AL.,
       Respondents.

ON WRIT OF CERTIORARI TO THE UNITED STATES
COURT OF APPEALS FOR THE TENTH CIRCUIT

BRIEF OF AMICI CURIAE 27+ LAY ROMAN
CATHOLICS IN SUPPORT OF RESPONDENTS

JAMES K. RILEY

INTERESTS OF THE AMICI CURIAE
         The amici, 27+ Lay Roman Catholic men and
women who are practicing members of the Roman
Catholic Church, support the actions of the
respondent State of Colorado. The decision below
which affirmed legislation prohibiting conversion
therapy directed towards individuals age18 years and
under should now be affirmed. 27+ Lay Roman
Catholics have submitted briefs amicus curiae to this
Court previously in support of LGBTQIA+ persons in
Fulton v. City of Philadelphia , 141 S.Ct. 1868 (2021)
and 303 Creative v. Elenis, 600 U.S. 570 (2023).1
SUMMARY OF THE ARGUMENT
         The legislation banning licensed medical
professionals from utilizing conversion therapy for
individuals aged 18 and under should not be set aside
on First Amendment grounds. Such treatment
regimens are inherently injurious to all, including
adults, and fail to accept LGBTQIA+ individuals with
closeness, compassion and tenderness in accord with
the teachings of Jesus Christ and the welcoming to all
“big tent” accompanying approaches to Christianity of
Pope Francis I.



1 Pursuant to Supreme Court Rule 37.6, counsel for  amici
curiae states that no counsel for a party authored this brief in
whole or in part  and no party or counsel for a party made a
monetary contribution intended to fund the preparation or
submission of this brief.

2

ARGUMENT
I.
“Conversion ‘therapy’ is not therapy, it is
abuse”  Vicky Brett
The amici are lay Roman Catholics with grave
concerns about serious adverse consequences from
“conversion therapy” (sometimes referred to as
“reparative therapy”) directed to persons of any age,
but especially to those age 18 years and under who
should never be dem onized nor judged as “perverted”
or “inadequate”. Such damning words are regularly
employed destructively in conversion therapy sessions
often with adverse impacts including self -
condemnatory ideation and compelled impressions of
worthlessness.
The amici contend that conversion therapy
should not be utilized even in the guise of religion, or
by religious counselors but, even more so it should
never be employed by medical practitioners or
therapists in secular settings. The Colorado
legislation exempts a person engaged in the practice
of religious ministry; it is aimed only at conversion
therapy delivered as purported medical treatment by
licensed therapists.
The amici support legislative prohibitions
applicable to licensed  medical professionals against
conversion therapy for persons under age
18. Amici, recognizing the risks of harm that
accompany such measures, also support such
prohibitions with regard to adult patients.

3

One must exercise great caution when
countenancing actions under religious beliefs when
there is significant risk that harm may result; religion
may be practiced but should not be in a weaponized
manner under the guise of scientifically based medical
practice by licensed professionals . That would be the
case here if licensed therapists are authorized to
institute conversion therapy. The risks that have been
identified in the scientific literature are compelling —
including risks of derogation of self-esteem, self-harm
and suicide. If such approaches are countenanced as
free speech, no governmental “guard -rails” would be
available to protect individuals from abuses.
One compelling anecdotal description (used
with permission) criticizing conversion therapy, was
presented by Vicky Brett, who is a Church of England
Lay Synod member and Lay Pioneer serving the
LGBTQIA+ community, with regard to the
experiences of her own child:
“The conversion therapy sometimes urged
on gay people by conservative Christians
is a very different matter from the kind of
listening and exploratory counselling
that should surely be the norm…”
She continues:
“A trained therapist does not tell you
what to think or what to do or who you
are – they allow you the freedom to
explore and question and understand
yourself and your situation. They do not
force or coerce you to transition or to not
transition. In contra st, the ‘Christian’

4

conversion practices we experienced held
not one jot of freedom or exploration – we
were told repeatedly that we were evil
and going to hell, that being transgender
or supporting someone was wrong, that
my child was a sexual pervert, that we
were bad paren ts, subjected to yelling
and prayer to remove demons…During
this time my child took an overdose, but
by God’s grace they were resuscitated….
Conversion ‘therapy’ is not therapy, it is
abuse.”
“Is the Conversion Therapy Ban a Muddle? A
Response to Angela Tilby”  by Vicky Brett, a member
of the House of Laity at General Synod and a Lay
Pioneer with the Church of England serving the
LGBTQIA+ community in Peterborough.
https://viamedia.news/2022/04/13/is-the-conversiontherapy-ban-a-muddle-a-response-to-angela-tilby/
II.
“…a sustained journey through Christian
history over the last two centuries reveals that
there is no such thing as a Christian theology
of sex.” Diarmaid MacCulloch
            Diarmaid MacCulloch, a fellow at St. Cross
College and Campion Hall, University of Oxford and
an emeritus professor of the history of the Church, as
well as an ordained deacon of the Church of England,
has recently completed an exhaustive  work “Lower
Than The Angels A History of Sex and Christianity”
(New York: 2024). It stands as an important
contribution in continuing  discussion concerning the

5

relationship between sex and gender and religion, in
particular of course Christianity. Mc Culloch
concludes in his closing chapter:
“Christian theology is not just a matter of
opening the Bible and reeling off a text or
learning Church dogma. It is dependent
on countless echoes of the past, back to
Greeks, Jews, even Hindus or
Buddhists.  The consequence is that
contrary to many assertions over the last
two centuries, a sustained journey
through Christian history reveals  that
there is no such thing as a Christian
theology of sex. There are multiple
Christian theologies of sex, many of
which have over t wo millennia been
downright contradictions of each other.
That shows no signs of changing…”
MacCulloch, “Lower Than The Angels”, pp.492-493.
III.
“To save people for their own good, whether
they know it or not.” Justice Antonin Scalia
In religious based efforts involving conversion
therapy, including those described by Vicky Brett and
crusading against  homosexuality as described i n
MacCulloch’s work,  the zealousness of well -
intentioned believers can have devastatingly negative
results. This approximates the concerns about
religious zealousness which Antonin Scalia in his
1989  address “Church and State” to the Pontifical
North American College in Rome, cautioned against:

6

“If one is a skeptic, or not entirely
convinced of the truth of one’s own
religious beliefs, it is quite easy to agree
that those beliefs should not be imposed,
and indeed should not even be fostered,
by the state.   After all, they might be
wrong. But for the Ayatollah Khomeni—
or, for that matter, for devout Christians
of the sort who managed the Inquisition,
the doctrine is more difficult. If one truly
believes that the hereafter is all
important, that the pleasures and griefs
of our 80 years or so in this  world are
insignificant except as a means of
entering the next, then the temptation is
to take  whatever action is necessary,
including coercive action by the state, to
save people for their own good, whether
they know it or not [Emphasis by
underline  added].”
Scalia Speaks Reflections on Law, Faith, and Life Well
Lived (2017)
IV.
Both Houses of Parliament of Canada By
Unanimous Actions Voted to Ban Conversion
Therapy For Adults As Well As Children
Canada, in 2022  by unanimous action
of both chambers of its Houses of Parliament
criminalized conversion therapy for persons
of any age. Canada’s prohibition received royal assent
on December 8, 2021 and thus became the law of the
nation of 30 days thereafter —“Statutes of Canada

7

2021—An Act To Amend the Criminal Code
(conversion therapy)”  www.ourcommons.ca. This
Court’s jurisprudence should include consideration of
international legislation especially when apropos and
compelling as with Canada’s action, here unanimously
undertaken, by a nation so closely aligned both
culturally and historically with our own. It is also
noteworthy that Canada regularly employs the
contraction or acronym “ LGBTQIA2”; the Arabic
number “2” is incorporated to recognize historic sex
and gender fluidity among indigenous peoples  which
has not been recognized to a similar extent to date in
the United States.
A significant number of other nations have a lso
passed prohibitions against conversion therapy  as
medical treatment—often directed at all persons —
both adults and adolescents . To repeat, in those
measures the prohibition lies against such treatment
for adults – not just for vulnerable adolescents.
Further, unlike the Colorado state law now being
considered, many of the prohibitions passed
internationally include criminal penalties. Wikipedia,
National bans of conversion therapy.
https://share.google./rYsRw1SgDr6T1C3QY
Amici must now respectfully inquire: —under
what premise would the Nation of Canada, and other
nations also, enact legislation prohibiting   conversion
or reparative therapy for adults as well as adolescents
(often with criminal sanctions) while state legislatures
in the United States would be barred from enacting
civil licensing prohibitions (even without criminal
sanctions) directed exclusively at secular licensed
medical practitioners relating only to the identified

8

vulnerable population of individuals aged 18 and
under?
CONCLUSION
For all reasons set forth herein, the decision
below should be affirmed.
Respectfully submitted,
James K. Riley
